translationRepairs: Li Tan, styled Songsou, was from Weizhou and was the son of Li Quan.
Li Tan, whose childhood name was Songsou, was from Weizhou and was the son of Li Quan.
s0001 has 小字松壽, a childhood name, not a courtesy style (字). The before text's styled mislabels the name kind; the proposed childhood-name wording matches the Chinese.

On the gengyin day Tan mobilized on his own to repair Yidu's walls and reported a Song attack on Lianshui. The court sent Azhu, Harabatu, Aixianbuhua, and others with full forces and told Du Yi to reinforce the mobilization as needed.

On the gengyin day Tan mobilized on his own to repair Yidu's walls and reported a Song attack on Lianshui. The court sent Azhu, Harabatu, Aixianbuhua, and others with full forces and further instructed that troops be increased for the mobilization as appropriate.

In 仍諭度宜益兵赴調, 度宜 is adverbial 'as appropriate', not a person named Du Yi. The proposed idiomatic correctly removes the invented name and restores the sense of increasing troops for mobilization as appropriate.

On gengyin day, Tan on his own authority dispatched troops to repair the walls and moats of Yidu, and also reported that Song troops were coming to attack Lianshui; an edict sent Azhu, Harabatu, and Aixianbuhua and others with all their troops to go there, and still instructed Du Yi to increase troops sent to the mobilization as appropriate.

On gengyin day, Tan on his own authority dispatched troops to repair the walls and moats of Yidu, and also reported that Song troops were coming to attack Lianshui; an edict sent Azhu, Harabatu, and Aixianbuhua and others with all their troops to go there, and still instructed that troops be increased and sent to the mobilization as appropriate.
The literal field invents the same false personal name from 度宜. The proposed replacement correctly treats 度宜 as 'as appropriate' and keeps 益兵赴調 as increasing troops sent to the mobilization.

Knowing the city would fall, Tan killed his favorite concubine with his own hand, took a boat onto Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the lake was shallow and he survived, was captured, bound, and brought before Prince Qubilai's tent.

Knowing the city would fall, Tan killed his favorite concubine with his own hand, took a boat onto Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the lake was shallow and he survived, was captured, bound, and brought before Prince Habichi's tent.
s0053 ends with 諸王合必赤帳前; 合必赤 is Prince Habichi, not Qubilai (忽必烈). The proposed idiomatic correctly names Habichi.

Tan knew the city was about to fall; he then personally killed his beloved concubine, boarded a boat into Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the water was shallow and he did not die, was captured by government troops, bound, and brought before the tent of Prince Qubilai.

Tan knew the city was about to fall; he then personally killed his beloved concubine, boarded a boat into Daming Lake, and threw himself into the water; the water was shallow and he did not die, was captured by government troops, bound, and brought before the tent of Prince Habichi.
The literal likewise misrenders 合必赤 as Qubilai. Habichi is the correct reading of the Chinese name in this unit.

Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhide, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.

Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhida, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.
s0131 dates the enfeoffment to 至大元年, the Zhida era, not Zhide. The proposed idiomatic correctly romanizes the era name.

Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhide, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.

Mieli begot Toqhu; Toqhu begot Andula; Andula begot Tuman. In the first year of Zhida, Tuman was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yangdi, granted a gold seal with dragon knob, and charged to guard the northern frontier.
The literal has the same Zhide error for 至大. Zhida is the correct romanization of the era in this sentence.
Soon Lao Zhang was further enfeoffed as Prince of Hening, made Liaobei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting Privy Council director, and charged with guarding the northern frontier.
Soon Lao Zhang was further enfeoffed as Prince of Hening, made Lingbei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting Privy Council director, and charged with guarding the northern frontier.
s0127 has 嶺北行省丞相, Lingbei Branch Secretariat, not Liaobei. The proposed idiomatic correctly restores Lingbei.

Shortly afterward an edict further enfeoffed Lao Zhang as Prince of Hening, with him as Liaobei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting as Privy Council director, ordering him to guard the northern frontier, it is said.

Shortly afterward an edict further enfeoffed Lao Zhang as Prince of Hening, with him as Lingbei Branch Secretariat chancellor acting as Privy Council director, ordering him to guard the northern frontier, it is said.
The literal likewise misreads 嶺北 as Liaobei. Lingbei is the accurate place-name reading for this office.
